summary: A 1883 cast-iron caisson tower at the mouth of the Providence River, Narragansett Bay's first offshore light; city-owned since 2004 and restored in 2024.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record's first_lit 1868 and built 1883 refer to the lit granite tower (1868) and the present iron tower (1883). The granite day beacon is dated 1857 by the NRHP and 1866 by LighthouseFriends; both say it was lit in 1868.
NRHP gives 1963; LighthouseFriends has the crew leaving 23 June 1965 and the USLHS roster runs to 1965. Story states the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Thin primary coverage: the local Light-House Board corpus starts 1891, so 1860s-80s construction details (appropriations, 1883 tower) rest on the NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends. The March 1875 ice account is the Daily Star of 9 March 1875 as quoted by LighthouseFriends (calls the station 'Conanicut'); not seen directly. The 1922 tragedy is told briefly and children are not named; AP OCR is poor, 'younger child died' rests on LighthouseFriends. The 1904 Pilgrim article is dated 19 Sept 'yesterday morning' so 18 Sept inferred. The 1921 Commissioner snippet page printed number unconfirmed; cited by scan page. The USCG roster lines (1957-65) are classified 'crew' by me. Possible Ernest L. Arnold / son 'Earnest' link not asserted. The 1916 Great Beds NJ link for Ellsworth Smith (LighthouseFriends) is not used. NRHP listing year not verified in a read source (register number implies 1988). Distance from shore: NRHP says one mile.
